# Protocols Used for Internet Access with FTTH (Fiber to the Home)

FTTH uses a **layered stack** of protocols depending on the network architecture. Here are the main ones:

## 1. Physical/Access Layer Protocols (PON Standards)
Most FTTH deployments use **Passive Optical Network (PON)** technology:

- **GPON** (Gigabit PON) – ITU-T G.984, up to 2.5 Gbps down / 1.25 Gbps up
- **XG-PON / XGS-PON** – 10 Gbps (symmetric in XGS)
- **EPON** (Ethernet PON) – IEEE 802.3ah, 1 Gbps
- **10G-EPON** – IEEE 802.3av
- **NG-PON2** – 40 Gbps using multiple wavelengths
- **25G/50G PON** – newer standards

Some deployments use **Active Ethernet (Point-to-Point)** instead, using standard Ethernet (IEEE 802.3).

## 2. Data Link Layer
- **Ethernet (IEEE 802.3)** – framing once converted from PON
- **GEM** (GPON Encapsulation Method) – inside GPON
- **VLAN tagging (802.1Q)** – often used to separate services (Internet, IPTV, VoIP)

## 3. Authentication / Session Protocols
- **PPPoE** (Point-to-Point Protocol over Ethernet) – very common for user authentication and IP assignment
- **IPoE** (IP over Ethernet) with **DHCP** – increasingly used as an alternative
- **802.1X** – sometimes for authentication

## 4. Network Layer
- **IPv4** and **IPv6** (often dual-stack)

## 5. Transport / Application Layer
- **TCP/UDP**, **HTTP/HTTPS**, **DNS**, etc. (standard internet protocols)

## Typical Flow
```
[ONT at home] → GPON/XGS-PON → [OLT at ISP] → Ethernet/IP → PPPoE/IPoE session → Internet
```

**In short:** The fiber access typically runs **GPON or XGS-PON**, with **PPPoE or IPoE/DHCP** handling user authentication over Ethernet, then standard **TCP/IP** for the actual internet traffic.
